purpose: Contract governance, SDK distribution and cross-repository compatibility. Not a runtime gateway.

authority: Testagram-native access-token issuance and live-session validation
services.auth: Testagram-native short-lived access JWT; PostgreSQL session/account checks on every protected request; opaque rotating refresh token accepted only by /api/auth/refresh; no external identity-provider bearer fallback on end-user routes
services.notes: Backend is the sole public product API and canonical identity authority. Mainline issues native Testagram sessions and checks PostgreSQL session/account state; legacy external-provider identifiers remain only as explicit reconciliation inputs and are not accepted as user bearer credentials. Admin Console staff sessions use the native Backend identity plus the encrypted testagram-staff cookie and PostgreSQL staff-role/MFA records. Registration remains fail-closed until private evidence, email, independent review and provisioning gates are enabled and accepted.

authority: Testagram-native login, refresh, recovery and session restoration
services.auth: Uses Backend-native login and rotating refresh credentials; stores only the refresh token in platform secure storage; access token stays in memory
services.notes: Flutter uses the Testagram-native Backend auth client for login, password recovery/reset, session restore, refresh and logout. It calls only the Backend public API with the short-lived native access token. Applicant and verification-session tokens are limited to their own identity operations; the native password is set only after approved provisioning. No foreign-provider bearer token is sent by the public client. Flutter must never receive service tokens, storage-provider keys, database credentials or private service URLs.

services.auth: PLATFORM_INTERNAL_TOKEN for protected platform writes; video and notification user routes validate Backend-native access JWTs against live PostgreSQL session/account state; user tokens are never platform service credentials
services.notes: Data Centre PR #93 adds the private identity-evidence namespace to the existing B2-primary/R2-replica media lifecycle, a separate identity-evidence service token, authenticated readiness, ownership-bound reviewer retrieval/deletion, migration 003 and a manual live-provider smoke. Backend PR #360 adds a dedicated identity-evidence client using its own service credential and the /internal/v1/identity-evidence/ route family; general media credentials cannot cross into this namespace. Both PRs are merged and their repository CI passed. The guarded B2/R2 staging smoke has not yet run, and the optional Data Centre media profile remains unaccepted for runtime activation until actual staging write/read/hash/replication/restore/delete evidence passes. Keep DATA_CENTRE_MEDIA_ENABLED and FRESH_MEDIA_ENABLED at their reviewed safe values until the separate media lifecycle gates pass. The legacy Fresh preview remains separately isolated and is not a supported identity or media fallback. User-aware video and notification routes continue to validate Backend-native JWTs against live PostgreSQL session/account state; service tokens remain separate.

services.auth: Backend-issued short-lived viewer assertion for private media; separate origin and purge credentials; raw user access JWT is not forwarded as a CDN origin credential
services.notes: Backend PR #223 is merged. It replaces the legacy Nginx cache with the immutable Go CDN image (sha256:e4c014a043b761d6f84b05d3973a3a6831522b863eef08685b7ca6db17f55ce9), a persistent bounded cache, private Backend origin, distinct origin/viewer-assertion/purge credentials and cache purge-before-delete. Backend origin-matrix tests, Go security checks, race/static tests and self-hosted Compose validation passed pre-merge. The merged Backend deployment workflow's input-validation job succeeded, but its actual deploy job was skipped; no live Go CDN service or external HTTPS acceptance is evidenced. CDN issues #61/#65 previously reported media.testagram.site serving the older R2 Worker; custom-domain/DNS cutover and rollback still require direct verification. Cloudflare deployment/DNS credentials are not available through the current repository integration. CDN viewer assertions remain distinct from user access JWTs and origin/purge credentials; CDN never becomes the identity or visibility authority.

authority: signed delivery of Backend-authorized public Create activities
public dereferencing of Backend-canonical ActivityPub Notes
services.auth: Public ActivityPub ingress uses HTTP Signatures; Backend-to-Federation uses a distinct service bearer; Federation-to-Backend uses a different service bearer
services.notes: Backend publishes authorized activities to the private /internal/v1/activities ingress using a dedicated direction-specific service bearer and activity ID idempotency key. Federation authenticates the ingress, verifies Backend actor eligibility, durably enqueues the outbox item and acknowledges 202 only after acceptance. Federation-to-Backend uses a separate bearer. Public routing, inbound activity projections, delivery workers and external-peer interoperability remain gated; durable acceptance is not proof of delivery.

authority: ranking order and ranking scores only
services.notes: Backend submits at most 200 already-authorized candidates to POST /v1/feed/rank and requests at most 50 results. The pinned Backend client and Algorithm OpenAPI agree on the path and API-version/service-bearer headers. Backend rejects unknown/duplicate IDs and rechecks current authorization before hydration. Staging service-authentication, timeout/fallback and load acceptance remain required.
